newsitem.title: UK: BREWING GIANTS TO REVAMP ALCOPOPS ADVERTS - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: BREWING GIANTS TO REVAMP ALCOPOPS ADVERTS - REPORT.

text.p: UK brewing giants are planning an overhaul of advertising campaigns for their controversial alcoholic sodas or "alcopops", specifically pitching the drinks at an adult market, The Independent said on Friday.
The report said Bass Plc, maker of Hoopers Hooch and Scottish Courage, maker of the Two Dogs alcoholic lemonade drinks, both hope the new advertising campaigns will deflect mounting criticism.
Alcopops have been attacked for encouraging under-aged drinking, prompting many supermarkets and pub groups to stop selling the drinks.
Bass will launch a multi-million stg advertising campaign and Scottish Courage plans to spend one million emphasising alcopops as adult drinks and targeting the female market in particular.
Bass is considering removing the cartoon character on its bottles in a repackaging as part of efforts to clean up the image, said the report.
The alcopops market has seen explosive growth since being introduced in 1996, with more than one hundred brands and a market estimated at 350 million stg.
